Heard the learned Senior counsel appearing for the writ petitioner and the learned Deputy Solicitor General appearing for the first respondent and the learned Standing counsel appearing for the second respondent and the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for respondents 3 and 4.
2.
The lands belonging to the petitioner were acquired under the provisions of the National Highways Act for road widening.
It is not in dispute that the award has already been passed for the land.
The learned Deputy Solicitor General informed the Court that on account of the pendency of the writ proceedings, decision could not be taken for close to 5 years.
Recently, the decision was taken.
They noticed that there are standing trees.

They have been duly noted down and it is formally P.Kaliappan vs The Government Of India on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54834381/
2 asserted by the Deputy Solicitor General.

I direct the fourth respondent to pass an award valuing the trees that stood on the petition-mentioned land and also disburse the award amount within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
4. With this direction to the respondents, this writ petition stands disposed of.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
It is now further undertaken that the award amount for the standing trees will be deposited in the petitioner's account.
It is stated that award will be passed very shortly.
I direct the fourth respondent to pass an award valuing the trees that stood on the petition-mentioned land and also disburse the award amount within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
4. With this direction to the respondents, this writ petition stands disposed of.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
